design_rules: Manipulate the represented prior-benefit event only: one member contains a concrete benefit directed to the focal person and the other contains a matched neutral contact with no benefit. Do not add an interpretation of either event.

Keep the two versions of every pair matched on the complete current-request block, actor relationship, need, effort, status, likability, familiarity, authority, setting, optionality, sentence structure, and terminal processing instruction; only the concrete prior exchange may differ.

Use a genuinely neutral prior-contact control: write observable contact actions in both members, with the no-reciprocal member showing completed, ordinary, observable contact such as a greeting or neutral conversation, with no benefit transfer or attempted transfer. Never use withholding, failed, refused, declined, unaccepted, incomplete, or merely proximate transfer scenes. The reciprocal member differs only by replacing that contact span with an actual completed transfer of a concrete benefit to the focal person.

Reject neutral-contact wording such as `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, `offered but`, or any equivalent that implies a withheld or failed offer, an unaccepted transfer, or mere proximity. The only pair-level event difference is whether the concrete benefit is actually transferred to the focal person.

Copy the current-request block verbatim across each pair, including requester need, effort, actor roles, social attributes, authority status, and response framing. No condition-dependent wording may occur outside the prior-exchange block.
Do not vary social status, likability, familiarity, popularity, general helpfulness, politeness, perceived fairness, or social norms across conditions.

Use a neutral wrapper around the scenario. Treat the registered probe template as a processing instruction, not prose to copy: do not put a theory interpretation in the wrapper or scenario, and end every prompt exactly with the verbatim suffix `Continue processing the scenario.`.

In paired probes, the two prompt texts must have the same terminal suffix and the same neutral current-request/contact framing; no sentence may be added, removed, or rephrased outside the short concrete prior-exchange span.
Do not use the construct ID, condition IDs, or condition labels in prompt_text.
Probe, behavior, steering, and calibration pools must use disjoint actors, events, and domains.
Do not infer or alter the preregistered readout sign from generated prose.

neutral_contact_contract.required: completed ordinary observable contact, such as a greeting or neutral conversation, with no benefit transfer
neutral_contact_contract.prohibited: withheld, failed, refused, declined, attempted, incomplete, unaccepted, or merely proximate transfer
neutral_contact_contract.benefit_member: actual completed transfer of a concrete benefit to the focal person

reject_if: the no-reciprocal member describes an attempted, withheld, failed, refused, declined, incomplete, or unaccepted benefit transfer
the no-reciprocal member uses mere or merely proximate contact or placement instead of genuinely neutral observable contact
the no-reciprocal member contains `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, or an equivalent cue
the reciprocal member does not contain an actual completed benefit transfer to the focal person
any text outside the short prior-contact span differs, including the current-request block or social attributes
the pair is not a closely length-matched minimal contrast

rejection_criteria: Reject any probe prompt_text whose final characters are not exactly `Continue processing the scenario.`.
Reject any prompt_text that contains the suffix before its final occurrence or has any character or text after the suffix, including notes, condition labels, or interpretation instructions.
Reject any no-reciprocal member that depicts a withheld, failed, refused, declined, attempted, incomplete, or unaccepted transfer rather than completed neutral observable contact.
Reject any no-reciprocal member that places or leaves a benefit beside, near, or within reach of the focal person, or relies on mere proximity instead of neutral contact.
Reject any pair containing `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, `offered but`, or an equivalent failed-offer or withholding cue in the neutral member.
Reject any reciprocal member without an actual completed transfer of a concrete benefit directed to the focal person.

Reject any pair when actors, time, setting, relationship, current request, need, effort, authority, social attributes, optionality, response framing, or terminal suffix differ outside the prior-contact span.
Reject any pair whose normalized prompt texts are not identical after replacing only the short prior-contact span, or that is not a closely length-matched minimal contrast.
Reject any prompt that omits the registered wrapper or uses a condition ID, construct name, or forbidden label in prompt_text.

behavior_factor_schedule.note: Cross prior-help magnitude, requester need, and effort cost independently in behavior_eval and steering_eval.
behavior_factor_schedule.balance_check: Each combination must appear once per behavior and steering content pool.

cells.instructions: Generate the configured number of matched pairs of short interpersonal scenarios. Use one fixed scenario skeleton per pair. In one member, describe an actual completed transfer of a concrete benefit directed to the focal person; in the other, describe completed ordinary observable neutral contact such as a greeting or neutral conversation, with no benefit transfer. This concrete prior-exchange span is the only condition-dependent edit. The neutral member must not depict a withheld, failed, refused, declined, attempted, incomplete, unaccepted, or merely proximate transfer; reject cues such as `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, or `offered but`. Copy the complete neutral current-request block, actor relationship, need, effort, setting, authority, status, likability, familiarity, optionality, sentence structure, wrapper, and terminal suffix verbatim across both members. Use observable actions only: never state a social norm, interpretation, expectation, obligation, duty, fairness judgment, or what anyone should do because of the prior contact. End every prompt exactly with `Continue processing the scenario.` and do not state the condition label.

Generate the configured number of new matched pairs in held-apart domains. Use one fixed skeleton and a short concrete prior-exchange span: one member contains an actual completed benefit transfer to the focal person and the other contains completed ordinary observable neutral contact with no benefit transfer. The neutral contact must not be a withheld, failed, refused, declined, attempted, incomplete, unaccepted, or merely proximate transfer; reject `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, and `offered but` cues. Copy the full current request and all nuisance factors verbatim within each pair, including actors, roles, need, effort, authority, status, likability, familiarity, setting, optionality, response framing, sentence order, and terminal suffix. Do not explain the meaning of the prior exchange or use social-norm, expectation, obligation, repayment, or duty language. End every prompt exactly with `Continue processing the scenario.`.

Generate the configured number of novel held-out matched pairs, avoiding train and validation entities and wording. Change only the concrete prior-exchange span: one member has an actual completed benefit transfer directed to the focal person and the matched member has completed ordinary observable neutral contact with no transfer. The neutral member must not use withholding, failed-offer, refusal, attempted, incomplete, unaccepted, placement, or proximity cues, including `did not hand`, `placed beside`, `kept from`, or `offered but`. Keep the complete current-request block and every nuisance factor identical, including need, effort, relationship, authority, status, likability, familiarity, setting, optionality, response framing, sentence structure, and terminal suffix. Do not write an interpretation or social norm about either contact; forbid expectation, obligation, repayment, duty, and reason-to-respond language. End every prompt exactly with `Continue processing the scenario.`.

Generate exactly one new-domain help-allocation item for each required combination. Include a prior helper and another requester with matched status, likability, familiarity, and neutral prior contact, ask for two integer allocations summing to 100, and never ask the model to label reciprocity.

Generate exactly one independent held-out help-allocation item for each required combination, with social attributes and neutral prior contact matched. Content must be distinct from behavior_eval and every probe pool.

Generate neutral help-allocation items with a small prior-help event, matched status, likability, familiarity, and neutral prior contact, used only to estimate within-cell output variation. Vary only requester need and effort cost; do not cue reciprocity or reuse behavior or steering content.
